    About the CNC Virtual Lab
    
  
    
    
    The CNC Virtual Lab is a hands-on simulator for learning CNC programming without a machine. You write a part program, press Run, and watch a virtual CNC lathe or vertical milling machine cut the workpiece. Every move removes material in the model, so the finished shape shows exactly what your program does.
    
    
    What you can do
    
    
      
      
    • Program in G-code (the CNC part program) or in APT. APT is translated to G-code and run on the same machine.
      • 
      
    • Watch tool motion, chips, coolant and spindle rotation, and read position, feed, speed, cutting speed, time, removed volume and spindle load.
      • 
      
    • Learn from crashes: rapid moves into the part, the chuck or vise, and cutting with the spindle off all raise an alarm.
      • 
      
    • Measure the part by tapping it, and use Check part to compare it with tolerances.
      • 
      
    • Open Analysis for cycle-time breakdown, tool usage, cutting data and spindle-load charts.
      • 
      
    • Open BOM for the bill of material: raw stock, tools, machine time and a cost estimate.
      • 
      
    • Open Worksheet for a printable lab worksheet with calculations, questions and observations.
      • 
      
    • Register or log in as a student, faculty member or administrator. Students can print their exercise report with their own details. The administrator keeps the records and can add or delete users.
      • 
      
    • The first time the lab is opened on a device, a short Setup wizard prepares the local workspace. Run it again any time from Help > Run setup wizard again.
      • 
    
    
    
    Two ways to work
    
    
      
      
    • Guided exercises. Six lathe and six mill exercises, each with a starter program and a working solution in G-code and APT.
      • 
      
    • Your own problem. Choose Custom: your own problem in the Exercise menu. Enter the block size, material, tools and machine limits, optionally a target outline and check points, then write a program and run it.
      • 
    
    
    
    Using the menu bar
    
    
      
      
    • File: reset the machine, load a starter or solution, open or save a program, copy it, print.
      • 
      
    • Machine: switch between the lathe and the mill.
      • 
      
    • Exercise: pick one of the six exercises for the selected machine, or your own problem.
      • 
      
    • Simulate: run, pause, step, reset, choose the speed and the view.
      • 
      
    • Analysis, BOM, Worksheet: open the report pages for the current exercise.
      • 
      
    • Help: this page, the User Manual and the Copyright notice.
      • 
    
    
    
    Good to know
    
    
    This is a teaching tool. It follows real programming rules, but it is not a certified machine simulator. Cutting data such as speeds, feeds, spindle load, energy and cost figures are for learning and are not production values.

    Accounts and stored data
    
    
    Registration details, passwords (stored only as salted hashes) and exercise progress are kept in the web-browser storage of the computer or phone on which the lab is used. They are not sent to any server. The administrator can export and import the records from the Admin console.
